summary: GATE VERDICT: proceed_with_review. trace-requirements-to-contracts is exceptionally well specified (11 ADDED requirements, 21 WHEN/THEN scenarios, 41 sized tasks each linked to a spec scenario and a design decision, 12 numbered design decisions, a JSON-Schema contract, and per-package verification commands with expected exit codes), so its outcomes are objectively checkable. Risk is low and reversible: no DB migration, zero external deps, file-level write_allow per package, and the gate itself defaults to opt-in ('untraced' does not fail). The 'has_security_signal' flag is a keyword false positive on the words 'author'/'authored' in the proposal and contract prose - no credentials, auth code, secrets, or permission logic are touched. VAL_REVIEW is recommended (not escalation) because this change lands a NEW BLOCKING CI gate and edits two shared skills, and because one concrete work-package scope gap was found: wp-model edits descriptor.py / service_descriptor.py, which feed two byte-identity --check gates in CI whose output paths are not in its write_allow.
completed_work: Read proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, work-packages.yaml, specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md, and contracts/ (traceability.schema.json, README.md) in the managed worktree.

Verified VERIFIABILITY: 11 ADDED requirements, 21 named scenarios, 42 WHEN/THEN clauses, 41 checkbox tasks across 5 phases, all tasks sized XS/S/M with no L or XL, per-task 'Spec scenarios' and 'Design decisions' back-references, and a JSON-Schema contract for the traceability block.

Verified RISK signals against the artifacts: has_db_migration false (confirmed - no alembic/migration surface), external_dep_count 0 (confirmed - gate is a static read of two files, no coordinator runtime dependency, no npm dependency at gate runtime), has_broad_write_scope false (confirmed - each of the 3 packages declares explicit file-level write_allow plus deny on agent-coordinator/**, openspec/specs/**, and openspec/contracts/** for wp-gate).

Traced the has_security_signal:true flag to its source: keyword matches on 'author'/'authored' in proposal.md, work-packages.yaml, spec.md and contracts/README.md. No secret, credential, token, password, auth, or permission surface exists in this change.

Verified the hard prerequisite is satisfied: derive-descriptors-from-contracts is archived at openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-28-derive-descriptors-from-contracts, and its code artifacts exist on this branch (openspec/contracts/ layout with 5 capabilities, packages/gen-eval/scripts/check_coverage_completeness.py, descriptor.py, service_descriptor.py).

Confirmed the DAG shape: wp-resolver -> wp-model -> wp-gate is a genuine chain (shared file packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/traceability.py, shared lock key feature:gen-eval:traceability), not an artificially serialized plan.

Confirmed the plan self-imposes the gates-must-fail-before-work rule (acceptance outcome, wp-gate description, tasks 4.3 and the final checkpoint), including the __pycache__ clearing note that the mutation-check staleness lesson requires.

decisions.rationale: Verifiability is above the bar and risk is low, so escalation is unwarranted. But the change installs a NEW BLOCKING CI gate at /validate-feature (task 5.6) and on main (task 5.7), and rewires skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md and skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md. The characteristic failure mode of this change class - a gate that can only ever pass, or a gate that blocks unrelated work on pre-existing debt - is precisely what the extra VAL_REVIEW phase catches, and it is cheap relative to landing a broken gate on the shared workflow.

decisions.decision: Not escalating despite total_loc_estimate 1850 and has_security_signal true.
decisions.rationale: Raw size is explicitly not the gate criterion, and 1850 LOC across 3 packages is well-specified rather than large-and-vague. The security signal is a false positive on the substring 'author'. Neither is an escalation cause.

The work is almost entirely new files under packages/gen-eval/. The gate defaults to opt-in per capability (D6: a capability with no traceability block records 'untraced' and does not fail), so landing it does not retroactively break existing capabilities. There is no data migration and no runtime coupling; a bad gate reverts in one commit. The mandatory human merge gate is the final backstop.

decisions.decision: Flagging - not blocking on - a work-package scope gap in wp-model.
decisions.rationale: wp-model's write_allow includes packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/descriptor.py and service_descriptor.py. Two CI steps assert byte identity against artifacts derived from those models: generate_contract_schemas.py --check (output packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/) at ci.yml:411 and generate_tool_descriptor.py --check (output packages/gen-eval/evaluation/descriptor.yaml) at ci.yml:431. Neither output path is in wp-model's write_allow, so adding a traceability field to the descriptor models will red those gates with the implementer unable to regenerate in scope. This is the known write_allow-misses-invalidated-files pattern; it is a scope-tuning fix for the implement phase, not a reason to stop for a human.

decisions.decision: Flagging that tasks.md phases 4 and 5 are deliberately NOT work packages.
decisions.rationale: work-packages.yaml states explicitly that phases 4 and 5 are human-led authoring work, because the gate cannot distinguish a considered citation from a guessed one (D1). tasks.md nonetheless contains tasks 4.1-5.9, so an implement phase driven from tasks.md rather than work-packages.yaml could dispatch citation authoring to an agent - which would produce exactly the plausible-looking mapping D1 forbids. The implement phase must treat work-packages.yaml as the dispatch authority.

next_steps: Proceed to PLAN_REVIEW, then IMPLEMENT with the 3-package chain wp-resolver -> wp-model -> wp-gate as declared in work-packages.yaml.

Before dispatching wp-model, widen its write_allow to include packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/** and packages/gen-eval/evaluation/descriptor.yaml, or add an explicit regeneration step, so the two byte-identity --check gates in ci.yml (lines 411 and 431) can be kept green.
Dispatch ONLY wp-resolver, wp-model, and wp-gate. Do not dispatch tasks 4.1-5.9 to implementer agents; they are human-led authoring work per work-packages.yaml.

Enforce the plan's own gates-must-fail-before-work rule during IMPL_REVIEW: every check in check_traceability.py must be demonstrated red on an unmodified tree, with __pycache__ cleared before each confirming run.
Run VAL_REVIEW (val_review_enabled is already true in state). Give it Bash so it can independently execute the gate against the real tree rather than trusting the implementer's report.

At VALIDATE, confirm the change-scoped run proves BOTH halves of task 3.13 (touched violation fails, untouched pre-existing gap reported and does not fail) - a test asserting only the first passes against a gate with no scoping at all.
